articles.title: Article: Securing Autonomous AI Agents on Kubernetes: Trust Boundaries, Secrets, and Observability for a New Category of Cloud Workload
articles.reason: The article provides production-ready security and observability patterns for deploying autonomous AI agents—directly relevant for building secure, compliant agentic workflows on Azure Container Apps or Kubernetes for enterprise clients.
articles.summary: This article details practical security architectures for running autonomous AI agents on Kubernetes, including job-based isolation, dynamic credential management with Vault, and phased trust models. It addresses real-world challenges like unpredictable agent behavior and multi-domain secrets, which are critical for enterprise-grade deployments. The observability strategies for non-deterministic agent cycles are especially useful for monitoring and compliance in regulated industries.
actionable_insights: Adopt job-based isolation and short-lived credentials (e.g., Vault) for agent workflows to minimize lateral movement and credential leakage.
Implement a phased trust model (shadow to autonomous) to safely roll out agentic systems in production environments.
Enhance observability pipelines to track and audit non-deterministic agent reasoning cycles for compliance and troubleshooting.

articles.title: What is Tokenization Drift and How to Fix It?
articles.reason: Tokenization drift can silently break RAG and agentic workflows in production, directly impacting reliability for enterprise deployments.
articles.summary: This article explains how subtle changes in tokenization can cause unexpected model degradation, even when data and code remain unchanged. It highlights the risks of tokenization drift in LLM pipelines, which is critical for maintaining stable performance in production RAG and agentic systems. The piece offers practical strategies to detect and mitigate these issues, which is directly relevant for consultants building robust GenAI solutions.
actionable_insights: Audit your current RAG and agentic pipelines for potential tokenization inconsistencies, especially after model or library updates.
